d: When Magnus Carlsen makes a move, the chess world tends to pay attention. But his decision to forfeit a final game at the Total Chess World Championship Tour after already winning his match has now been followed by other players, turning an individual choice into a wider debate about sportsmanship and tournament rules. Bibisara Assaubayeva and R Vaishali were left without the chance to play those final games, while FIDE has been forced to confront an uncomfortable question about its own regulations. Is Carlsen setting a poor example, or simply using the rules to his advantage? Rupha Ramani…
